text: Councilman/Business Owner
I have been your advocate for change in Brea politics and accomplished much with one vote against an unresponsive Council majority. Help me to keep accountability and transparency, front and center.

As your advocate, I helped pass Measure T, removing benefits for part-time Councilmembers. I established case law in government accountability by defending citizens’ rights regarding ballot initiatives (Vargas vs. Balz). I consistently vote against tax, and fee increases which impacts our seniors and small businesses. I vote No to water rate increases which are unwarranted, Brea owns 1/3rd of the water company.

Since 2016, I have spearheaded the Integrated Crime Center to fully utilize technology to improve crime prevention and investigations to keep Brea safe. Partnering with our City Treasurer; we found billing errors by a city contractor, thousands have been recovered, with action pending to prevent future abuses.

My decades long commitment to public service includes 27-years military experience; Iraq war veteran, civil engineering corps Lieutenant Commander (retired) with master’s degree in public administration.

I will work diligently to continue to earn your trust. Contact me directly by cell: 714-306-4523 or email: votevargas@gmail.com. Please Vote Vargas; strength and experience you can depend on. Your vote matters!

text: Councilmember/Business Owner
As your Councilmember, I have focused on protecting Brea's future through:
Strong Public Safety
Responsible Leadership
Sound Fiscal Management

I helped arrange the purchase of three new fire engines and one ladder truck to strengthen emergency response and ensure our firefighters have the equipment they need to serve our community. I also secured a grant to establish an Integrated Crime Center, enhancing public safety by providing law enforcement with advanced technology and real-time information to better prevent and respond to crime.

In addition, I helped secure more than $28 million in federal and state funding, bringing your tax dollars back to Brea to invest in local priorities rather than leaving them elsewhere. While many surrounding cities and others across California have sought new tax measures, I have worked to keep Brea financially strong without asking residents for additional taxes.

During my time on the City Council, Brea has maintained a balanced budget and a 25% reserve, ensuring long-term fiscal stability and preparedness for future challenges. I remain committed to protecting taxpayers, strengthening public safety, and preserving the high quality of life that makes Brea an exceptional place to live, work, and raise a family.
Please Vote Cecilia Hupp

text: Public Affairs Manager
My name is Blake Perez, and I respectfully ask for your vote for Brea City Council.

I am a homegrown candidate. For more than 26 years, Brea has been my home. I attended our public schools, from Arovista Elementary to Brea Olinda High School. I earned my Eagle Scout award with a local troop. I am completely shaped by this community. And now I am working hard to raise my daughter in this community too. And I am running to make sure her future can be shaped by a Brea just as great as I had.

My priorities are safe neighborhoods, a strong local economy, and livable infrastructure, all grounded in fiscal responsibility, transparency, and meaningful community engagement. Those are the fundamentals of good local government, and they will guide every decision I make.

Professionally, I serve as a Public Affairs Manager, working with local governments, businesses, and community organizations to solve problems, build partnerships, and deliver practical results. I have also served Brea for the past eight years on the Cultural Arts Commission and Planning Commission.
Together, we can prepare Brea for the future while protecting what makes it special today.

text: Consumer Relations Manager
Hello Brea, my name is Andrew Herrera or, as some of you may know me, the Enjoy Brea guy.

This is my second time running for City Council. My first campaign was a great learning experience, and I had the opportunity to meet many wonderful people. One piece of feedback I received was that I didn't know enough about the city. Another was that, while my platform focused on supporting small businesses, people wanted to know how I planned to do that.

Currently, I serve as vice president of the Brea Historical Society, where I have the opportunity to learn about our city's history from day one. Every day, I learn something new that makes me love Brea even more. Small businesses are the backbone of our economy, and for the past four years, I have spent my free time getting to know Brea business owners and sharing their services and stories with tens of thousands of people through my various volunteer platforms.
As a council member, my approach would be to gather input from the community before making decisions that affect us all. I want everyone to feel comfortable coming to me, knowing that I will listen.
